en: The Sūtra of the Eight Secret Names of the Buddha’s Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Minister Dharmaśrī (Fǎxián), Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee and Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, under Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
Furthermore, there was an assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
with Vajrapāṇi as their leader. At that time,
the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāguhyapati Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Just as your own family is called the Vajra Family,
among the most supreme and profound secret teachings within the Vidyādhara-piṭaka,
sentient beings possess shallow understanding and inferior faculties.
The secret meaning is difficult to believe and difficult to understand.
You have already spoken of a dharma that is difficult to believe and understand;
if you do not rely on the Dharma, you cannot be called a holy person.
He is named "Unwholesome" and is also called "Difficult to Subdue.
Vajrapāṇi, I shall now briefly explain to you within this Vajra Family your eight secret names and dhāraṇīs.
If one upholds and recites this dhāraṇī,
whatever they seek will be easily accomplished.
If a person hears this sūtra of the dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain success].
For those who, with a sincere heart, receive, uphold, read, and recite [this sutra],
all their karma of immediate retribution shall be completely extinguished;
this is due to the power of the Dharma when one upholds this sutra.
All eighty-four thousand koṭis of nayutas of evil māras will retreat, scatter,
and flee to the worlds of the ten directions.
If there are those who hear this dhāraṇī and rejoice with longing and aspiration, [they shall attain such merit].
This person who did not maintain the precepts attains the perfection of the precepts;
one who was not a practitioner of the holy life achieves the holy life;
one who was not tranquil achieves tranquility.
Eventually, they shall behold all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, who will joyfully comfort them and grant their requested aspirations so that they may achieve fulfillment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi received the Buddha’s reprimand.
Prostrating with his head at [the Buddha's] feet, he addressed him, saying, "World-Honored One,
what I previously stated is indeed in accordance with your holy intent.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will not abandon his great compassion."
For the sake of all sentient beings, both present and future,
I shall proclaim my eight secret names and dharanis,
so that all sentient beings may obtain great benefit.
The Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively!
Within the Vajra Family of the most excellent Vidyādhara-piṭaka,"
I shall proclaim your eight secret names:
first, Elephant Ear;
second, Sublime Adornment.
The third was named Guṇaratnasāgara; the fourth, Acala;
and the fifth, Satyamegha.
Sixth is named Lovely Form;
seventh is named Flame Light;
eighth is named Wondrous Color.
Vajrapāṇi, these are your eight secret names.
Then he spoke this dhāraṇī:

Namaḥ buddhāya | Namaḥ dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Namaḥ vajrapāṇaye | Tadyathā | Acche | Kharace | Sumomukhe | Sarvakāryanisādye | Hiri | Miri | Dhini | Siddhyantu mantrapadāni svāhā || The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Regarding these secret names and dhāraṇīs,
if there should be anyone who receives, maintains, reads, or recites them,
that person shall not fall into hell for seven koṭi-nayuta hundreds of thousands of kalpas; and at the time of their death, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas...
He manifested himself before them to comfort them with the teaching of the Dharma.
After his life ended, he was reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the other bodhisattvas,
as well as all the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and non-humans of the world,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Secret Eightfold Name Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha.
